justification: Dead-code removal. The Intelligence Brief had two copies of the fan-out/assembly logic: the batch run_intelligence_brief (POST /pipeline/intelligence-brief) and the streaming _generate_brief_sse (POST /pipeline/intelligence-brief/stream). Only the streaming path is used — the Trigger.dev relay (plotdetect-agents/trigger/intelligence-brief.ts) POSTs to /stream and the frontend consumes the SSE stream. The batch endpoint had zero callers anywhere; the only reference was test_brief_constraint_parity.py, which existed solely to babysit the two copies for drift. Removed the dead function, its route, and the obsolete parity test, and reworded two stale comments that named the deleted function. No logic, query, or schema change. One assembly path remains, eliminating the drift class that previously dropped the capacity headline from the live stream (fixed in #512).

break_it.scenario: Some other caller (e.g. an external API consumer) still POSTs to /pipeline/intelligence-brief (the removed batch route)
break_it.repro: grep the repo and the Trigger.dev relay for the route
break_it.how: verified zero callers: the only reference in-repo was the parity test (reads the function source); the Trigger.dev relay (plotdetect-agents/trigger/intelligence-brief.ts) POSTs to /pipeline/intelligence-brief/stream only (line 156); the frontend consumes the SSE stream; no other in-repo reference exists

break_it.scenario: The streaming path silently regresses without the parity test guarding it
break_it.what_happens: a brief section could go missing from the live stream undetected
break_it.how: the parity test only compared the now-deleted batch path against the stream; with one path it is obsolete. The remaining streaming assembly is covered by tests/test_intelligence_brief_schema.py and tests/test_intelligence_brief_orchestrator.py (157 pass), plus a live SSE smoke (metadata then 8 sections then complete, 0 errors)
